answers.question: Your answers say reads may be retried on timeout without limit. Nothing then ends a call to list the customer's orders that keeps getting no answer, and the conversation could go on forever. What ends it? Under the recommendation, the agent tries a list call at most three times; when all three get no answer, it treats the read as failed: at the start it says it cannot see the customer's orders right now and changes nothing, and after a cancel or refund call it follows your "re-read fails" answers. Claims put to the owner: C-07.
answers.recommended: The agent sends a list call at most three times in a row. When all three get no answer, the read has failed: at the start the agent says it cannot see the customer's orders right now and changes nothing; after a cancel or refund call it follows the "re-read fails" answers.
answers.reply:
No. The record says:
> Reads may be retried on timeout without limit; only commit calls are bounded.
> list_orders includes cancelled orders.
> Proposed set shown to the user: list_orders() (returns each order with its refund or null), cancel_order(order_number), issue_refund(order_number) (supplied), request_staff_followup(order_number, reason) with reasons refund_not_issued, refund_status_unknown, cancellation_unknown; terminal refund error returns a refund with status failed, transient error creates none; handoff timeout not retried; SG-02 (store staff work every follow-up task) added.
> Recommended: the customer is already signed in, and the agent sees only that customer's orders (a precondition).
> For case 3, after the retry the agent re-reads the refund record: pending or issued, report that status; failed or no refund, hand off and say the refund is not confirmed yet; re-read fails, say status unknown and hand off.
> If the cancel call times out: no blind resend; re-read the order.
> Re-read fails, say outcome unknown, issue no refund, hand off.
> Cancel succeeded, refund call timed out — state unknown; agent retries once, then re-reads the order and refund records and reports what it finds.

answers.question: Two outcomes your answers list without saying what the agent does. (a) The cancel call answers OrderNotFound for an order taken from the customer's own list. (b) The refund call answers OrderNotCancelled, after the agent saw the order cancelled. Under the recommendation, for (a) the agent says the order was not cancelled and no refund was issued, and sends no refund call; for (b) it sends no further refund call, tells the customer it is not known whether the order was cancelled and that no refund was issued, and creates a follow-up task with the reason cancellation unknown. Otherwise the agent would guess. Claims put to the owner: C-11, C-49.
answers.recommended: Yes to both: (a) the agent says the order was not cancelled and no refund was issued, and sends no refund call; (b) it sends no further refund call, tells the customer it is not known whether the order was cancelled and no refund was issued, and creates a follow-up task with the reason cancellation unknown.
answers.reply:
Yes, I accept your recommendation.
> cancel_order is idempotent (cancelling a cancelled order returns cancelled).
> Outcomes: cancelled; OrderNotCancellable{status} (replaces OrderShipped, covers shipped and delivered); OrderNotFound; timeout.
> An order number matching none of the customer's orders: the agent says so and changes nothing.
> Note the race: status can flip processing → shipped between the agent's read and its cancel call; the store rejects the cancel and the agent must report that truthfully and issue no refund call.
> issue_refund adds outcome OrderNotCancelled.
> Cancel succeeded, refund call returned an error — refund not issued, state known; agent reports it, does not claim success, hands off to the store's manual refund process.
> One retry allowed on a transient error, none on a terminal one.
> Tool contract: issue_refund(order_number) is idempotent, keyed on order number — repeated calls return the same refund id and never create a second refund.
> The agent may retry it.
> One handoff call covers both the failed-refund case and the unknown-cancellation case, with a reason argument.
> Proposed set shown to the user: list_orders() (returns each order with its refund or null), cancel_order(order_number), issue_refund(order_number) (supplied), request_staff_followup(order_number, reason) with reasons refund_not_issued, refund_status_unknown, cancellation_unknown; terminal refund error returns a refund with status failed, transient error creates none; handoff timeout not retried; SG-02 (store staff work every follow-up task) added.

answers.question: The follow-up task reasons are refund not issued, refund status unknown and cancellation unknown. When the refund call returns an amount that differs from the total the customer said yes to, the agent hands the case to staff. Which reason does it give? Claims put to the owner: C-48.
answers.reply:
Yes, I accept your recommendation.
> Proposed set shown to the user: list_orders() (returns each order with its refund or null), cancel_order(order_number), issue_refund(order_number) (supplied), request_staff_followup(order_number, reason) with reasons refund_not_issued, refund_status_unknown, cancellation_unknown; terminal refund error returns a refund with status failed, transient error creates none; handoff timeout not retried; SG-02 (store staff work every follow-up task) added.
> One handoff call covers both the failed-refund case and the unknown-cancellation case, with a reason argument.
> Rules, not fields: full-order cancellation only (no partial); refund amount = order total paid; refund payment method = order's payment method; at most one refund per order.
> Proposed default: the agent cancels an order only after the customer explicitly confirms the full proposal (which order, the refund amount and where it goes); any change after confirmation voids it.
> Proposed: the agent states one proposal (e.g. "cancel order HG-10482 and refund $86.40 to Visa ending 4242"); the customer's one "yes" authorizes both calls.
> Final message must match the final refund status.

answers.question: Two cases your answers leave open. (a) The second cancel call also gets no answer: under the recommendation the agent sends no third cancel call, says it is not known whether the order was cancelled and that no refund was issued, and creates a follow-up task with the reason cancellation unknown; otherwise it would re-read the order again. (b) The customer says yes, then changes the proposal (asks for a different amount or payment method): your answers say the change voids the yes. Under the recommendation the agent says the refund is the order's total paid to its payment method, and asks for a yes to the proposal again; otherwise it would end the conversation without cancelling. Claims put to the owner: C-38, C-47.
answers.recommended: Yes to both: (a) no third cancel call; the agent says the outcome is unknown, issues no refund and creates a follow-up task with the reason cancellation unknown; (b) the agent restates the proposal with the total paid to the order's payment method and asks for a yes again.
answers.reply:
No. The record says:
> If the cancel call times out: no blind resend; re-read the order.
> Cancelled, continue to refund.
> Still placed or processing, send the cancel once more under the same confirmation.
> Shipped, report it and issue no refund.
> Re-read fails, say outcome unknown, issue no refund, hand off.
> Reads may be retried on timeout without limit; only commit calls are bounded.
> cancel_order is idempotent (cancelling a cancelled order returns cancelled).
> Outcomes: cancelled; OrderNotCancellable{status} (replaces OrderShipped, covers shipped and delivered); OrderNotFound; timeout.
> One handoff call covers both the failed-refund case and the unknown-cancellation case, with a reason argument.
> Proposed set shown to the user: list_orders() (returns each order with its refund or null), cancel_order(order_number), issue_refund(order_number) (supplied), request_staff_followup(order_number, reason) with reasons refund_not_issued, refund_status_unknown, cancellation_unknown; terminal refund error returns a refund with status failed, transient error creates none; handoff timeout not retried; SG-02 (store staff work every follow-up task) added.
> Proposed default: the agent cancels an order only after the customer explicitly confirms the full proposal (which order, the refund amount and where it goes); any change after confirmation voids it.
> Proposed: the agent states one proposal (e.g. "cancel order HG-10482 and refund $86.40 to Visa ending 4242"); the customer's one "yes" authorizes both calls.
> Rules, not fields: full-order cancellation only (no partial); refund amount = order total paid; refund payment method = order's payment method; at most one refund per order.
